I didn't implement `title(text)`, because the frozen tests contradict the spec and can't both pass.

- `test_words` expects `title('hello world') == 'Hello World'`, which matches the spec.
- `test_three` expects `title('one two three') == 'One two Three'`. That leaves "two" lowercase, which contradicts "capitalise the first letter of every word".

No consistent rule fits both tests while following the spec. The only way to pass both would be to hard-code special behaviour, such as leaving the second word lowercase. That would work around the tests rather than implement the requested function.

Either the expected value in `test_three` should be `'One Two Three'`, or the spec is missing a rule. Tell me which and I'll implement it. The likely implementation is `' '.join(w.capitalize() for w in text.split(' '))`, which keeps the original spacing.
